questions.stem: For the unforced mass–spring–damper model m ẍ+b ẋ+kx=0 with m=1 kg, b=6 N·s/m and k=9 N/m, which pole/damping description is correct?

options.text: Two distinct negative real poles; overdamped.
A repeated pole at +3 s⁻¹; unstable.
A repeated pole at −3 s⁻¹; critically damped.

  Q.1 A mass-spring-damper system has 𝑚 = 1 𝑘𝑔, 𝑏 = 6 𝑁· 𝑠/𝑚, and

      𝑘 = 9 𝑁/𝑚. Based on the characteristic equation, what type of

        response does this system exhibit?

      A) Underdamped

       B) Overdamped

       C) Critically damped

      D) Unstable

       Answer: C

       Refer to Lecture 21: Linear Control of Manipulators Slide 11

         characteristic equation 𝑚𝑠² + 𝑏𝑠 + 𝑘 = 0

                             𝑠2 + 6𝑠+ 9 = 0

       𝑏2 = 62 = 36; 4𝑚𝑘= 4 × 1 × 9 = 36;

       𝑏2 = 4𝑚𝑘; critically damped system.


  Que  For a mass-spring-damper system with 𝑚 = 4, 𝑏 = 1, 𝑘 = 1, a
  2     control law 𝑓 = −𝑘ₚ𝑥 − 𝑘ᵥẋ  is applied to achieve a critically
      damped response with desired closed-loop stiffness 𝑘′ = 16. What
        are the values of 𝑘ₚ and 𝑘ᵥ respectively?
      A) 7, 15
       B) 15,7
       C) 7,7
      D) 15,15
       Answer: D
       Refer to Lecture 21: Linear Control of Manipulators Slide 19 for
        equations:

solution.justification: The zero discriminant and repeated negative pole establish critical damping.

optionExplanations.o4: The discriminant is zero, so there is no imaginary pair.
optionExplanations.o1: Critical damping gives coincident rather than distinct real poles.
optionExplanations.o2: The positive damping coefficient gives a negative repeated pole here.

assumptions: Linear scalar model with m,k>0 and no applied force.

solution.simpleExplanation: The zero discriminant and repeated negative pole establish critical damping.
misconceptions: Critical damping gives coincident rather than distinct real poles.
The positive damping coefficient gives a negative repeated pole here.
The discriminant is zero, so there is no imaginary pair.

Q.5  What  is the purpose of a "linearizing control law" in nonlinear

      control?

     A) To add more nonlinearity to the system for robustness

     B) To use a control input that cancels nonlinear effects, so the closed-

      loop system behaves in a simpler way

     C) To eliminate the need for feedback entirely

     D) No change in system dynamic model needed.

     Answer: B

     Refer to Lecture 23: Nonlinear and Time-Varying Systems Slide 8


Q.6  Compare a linear spring 𝑓1 (with constant 𝑘1) and a nonlinear spring
      𝑓2 = 𝑘2𝑥³ (with constant 𝑘2) both with coefficient value 10 (𝑘1 =
     10 𝑁/𝑚, 𝑘2 = 10 𝑁/𝑚³). At a displacement of 𝑥 = 2 m, what is the
       ratio of the nonlinear spring force to the linear spring force?

     Answer: 4

     Answer: 4

      Linear force, 𝑓1 = 𝑘1. 𝑥= 10 × 2 = 20 𝑁.
     Nonlinear force, 𝑓2 = 𝑘2. 𝑥³ = 10 × 2³ = 10 × 8 = 80 𝑁.

               𝑓2   80      Ratio,  =  = 4.
               𝑓1   20
